evidence_packet.evidence_text: Landlady says up to 60 teenagers attacked pub with fireworks - BBC News Image caption, Paula said she had to lock 30 customers inside her pub By Georgie Docker North West Published 4 November 2026 A landlady said she locked customers inside her pub for hours while a group of teenagers attacked it with fireworks. Salford pub manager Paula, 61, said she and 30 customers hid out as "about 60 teenagers" bombarded The Plough, in Cadishead, on Saturday. Police were called, and footage from the incident, appearing to show doors being kicked and a bus driver being assaulted, has since been shared on social media. "It was very scary. I'm worried they will come back," Paula said. Paula, who has been in charge at The Plough for 10 months, said she had "never seen anything like it", and that she feared the attack was "organised". "It started with just a few of them," she said. "But more starting coming and then there was 60 of them." Paula said the teenagers began by targeting "anyone passing" on the main road, including families out trick-or-treating. Greater Manchester Police Ch Insp Lee Gridley said the force would not "tolerate anti-social behaviour in our communities". "We will relentlessly tackle criminality, disrupt ASB and improve safety for local communities," he said. A force spokesperson said inquiries were ongoing to identify those responsible. Image caption, Paula said the incident followed a similar one where the gang had targeted doors on the high street The landlady said the pub became a target after she refused some teens use of the toilets, having told them children were not allowed in after 19:00. title: 'Floating tractors' clean up weed-choked waterways

evidence_packet.title: 'Floating tractors' clean up weed-choked waterways
evidence_packet.lead: Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 on a weed removal programme
evidence_packet.summary: Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 on a weed removal programme
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause problems for boats The weeds can also starve underwater plants of light and reduce levels of oxygen needed by fish and other wildlife, and can have a damaging impact on kingfishers and otters Kieran Howlett, from the Canal & River Trust, said managing the weeds was becoming more challenging but the charity was determined to protect the "wonderful waterways" With warmer summers and longer growing seasons, these fast-growing plants spread quickly through the canal network and can rapidly form a thick green carpet across the water's surface Described as "a bit like floating tractors" by the Canal & River Trust, the specialist machines cut and collect weeds from the water, helping the team remove about 30 tonnes each week

evidence_packet.summary: Transport bosses in Greater Manchester have confirmed there are no plans for a congestion charge in the city centre Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed plans to "invest heavily" in public transport instead of introducing a congestion charge, the Local Democracy Repo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport bosses in Greater Manchester have confirmed there are no plans for a congestion charge in the city centre Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed plans to "invest heavily" in public transport instead of introducing a congestion charge, the Local Democracy Reporting Service reported The transport agency said it will be investing invest £2.5bn of government money into the region between 2027 and 2032, and bringing trains to the Bee Network from December A report published by Manchester City Council on Tuesday revealed traffic had become so bad that it had cost the region's economy billions of pounds "There are no plans for a congestion charge in any part of Greater Manchester, instead we are investing heavily in the Bee Network to give people a reliable alternative to getting in their car," a TfGM spokesperson said "One tram full of people could replace around 200 cars on the road and a double decker bus around 75, demonstrating the benefits of getting more people on board the Bee Network."

title: Two more arrests in £1m university fraud investigation in Bolton

evidence_packet.title: Two more arrests in £1m university fraud investigation in Bolton
evidence_packet.lead: Two more arrests have been made in an investigation into £1m of alleged financial irregularities at the University of Greater Manchester, formerly named the University of Bolton, between 2014 and 2025 Two men, in their 50s and 60s, have been arrested on suspicion of witness intim
evidence_packet.summary: Two more arrests have been made in an investigation into £1m of alleged financial irregularities at the University of Greater Manchester, formerly named the University of Bolton, between 2014 and 2025 Two men, in their 50s and 60s, have been arrested on suspicion of witness intim
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two more arrests have been made in an investigation into £1m of alleged financial irregularities at the University of Greater Manchester, formerly named the University of Bolton, between 2014 and 2025 Two men, in their 50s and 60s, have been arrested on suspicion of witness intimidation, perverting the course of justice and fraud by the abuse of position after raids in Bolton and South Yorkshire, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said One of the men was previously arrested on suspicion of money laundering in July, along with another man and a woman GMP said it was "exploring evidence indicating over £1m worth of fraudulent activity", including 60 transactions and more than a million emails The force started the investigation last year into "serious allegations of fraud and bribery" at the university after a report by the Manchester Mill , external and a subsequent report from Price Waterhouse Cooper commissioned by the university's Fraud Response Panel Two men in their 60s and a woman in her 50s who were arrested in July were released on bail under investigation

evidence_packet.summary: A landlady said she locked customers inside her pub for hours while a group of teenagers attacked it with fireworks Salford pub manager Paula, 61, said she and 30 customers hid out as "about 60 teenagers" bombarded The Plough, in Cadishead, on Saturday Police were called, and foo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A landlady said she locked customers inside her pub for hours while a group of teenagers attacked it with fireworks Salford pub manager Paula, 61, said she and 30 customers hid out as "about 60 teenagers" bombarded The Plough, in Cadishead, on Saturday Police were called, and footage from the incident, appearing to show doors being kicked and a bus driver being assaulted, has since been shared on social media "It was very scary. I'm worried they will come back," Paula said Paula, who has been in charge at The Plough for 10 months, said she had "never seen anything like it", and that she feared the attack was "organised" "It started with just a few of them," she said. "But more starting coming and then there was 60 of them."

title: 'Floating tractors' clean up weed-choked waterways

evidence_packet.title: 'Floating tractors' clean up weed-choked waterways
evidence_packet.lead: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause p
evidence_packet.summary: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause p
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause problems for boats The weeds can also starve underwater plants of light and reduce levels of oxygen needed by fish and other wildlife, and can have a damaging impact on kingfishers and otters Kieran Howlett, from the Canal & River Trust, said managing the weeds was becoming more challenging but the charity was determined to protect the "wonderful waterways" With warmer summers and longer growing seasons, these fast-growing plants spread quickly through the canal network and can rapidly form a thick green carpet across the water's surface Described as "a bit like floating tractors" by the Canal & River Trust, the specialist machines cut and collect weeds from the water, helping the team remove about 30 tonnes each week

title: Ryanair passenger describes 'traumatic' Murcia flight bomb threat

evidence_packet.title: Ryanair passenger describes 'traumatic' Murcia flight bomb threat
evidence_packet.lead: The evacuation of a Ryanair aircraft after a suspected bomb threat has been described as "quite traumatic" by a passenger who was on board the flight Sarah Jones said police, fire crews and bomb disposal officers surrounded the plane after it landed at Murcia airport from Manches
evidence_packet.summary: The evacuation of a Ryanair aircraft after a suspected bomb threat has been described as "quite traumatic" by a passenger who was on board the flight Sarah Jones said police, fire crews and bomb disposal officers surrounded the plane after it landed at Murcia airport from Manches
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The evacuation of a Ryanair aircraft after a suspected bomb threat has been described as "quite traumatic" by a passenger who was on board the flight Sarah Jones said police, fire crews and bomb disposal officers surrounded the plane after it landed at Murcia airport from Manchester The medic from Manchester said she and her fellow passengers were told to leave their belongings on board and then spent about three hours in an airport hangar while the plane was searched Spanish officials said no explosives were found. The aircraft was one of seven searched at airports across Europe following a series of suspected bomb threats Jones was travelling with colleagues Charlotte and Kelly to work as medics at a golf tournament in La Manga in south-eastern Spain She said the flight was uneventful until the aircraft landed at about 10:30 local time (09:30 GMT)

Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of companies with debts by providing 'misleading services', the government's Insolvency Service has said The Manchester-registered company was found to be offering 'alternatives' to formal insolvency to directors of the companies in financial difficulty. It offered to arrange sales of 'financially distressed' businesses for £1 whilst charging fees of between £2,500 and £6,800 It comes following an Insolvency Service investigation which has subsequently led to the firm being shut down Insolvency Service Chief Investigator, David Usher, said: "Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of struggling businesses by offering directors a misleading route out of their company’s debts, charging thousands of pounds for the service "Selling a company does not prevent its former directors’ conduct from being investigated if it later enters liquidation

He spent hours playing in the streets of North Reddish , where he was brought up A big Manchester City fan, he played for his school at Stockport County's Edgeley Park and represented Stockport schoolboys. However, he says, by his late teens, 'reality started to hit' and he realised he would need to 'get into the world of work.' Aged just 18, he got a Saturday job at the BrightHouse furniture shop in Hyde , Tameside . It was the start of a remarkable career journey that has now seen him build his own empire of shops Dad-of-two James, now aged 38, is the founder of Mintro, which buys and sells pre-owned phones and technology, jewellery, watches and designer handbags, and which now has eight stores across the North West, including five in Greater Manchester He has done so alongside a fruitful football career which has seen him play for a number of local non-league sides, most notably Bury FC

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS More strikes expected at four Greater Manchester hospitals after staff reject pay offer Nearly all theatre staff voted to reject the Northern Care Alliance's offer Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Write More strikes are expected at a crisis-hit NHS trust after hundreds of theatre staff overwhelmingly rejected its latest offer in a long-running dispute over overtime pay Nearly all (99 per cent) of more than 400 theatre staff, including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers, working across four hospitals voted to reject the Northern Care Alliance's (NCA) offer The Trust, which runs Salford Royal, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Fairfield General Hospital in Bury , said it was "very disappointing" that workers had rejected what it described as its "best offer" to end the dispute Trade union Unison, which represents the striking workers, said staff had sent a "resounding message" to NCA bosses and confirmed staff would continue to strike The dispute centres on the use of an outside agency called NHS Professionals (NHSP) to manage additional shifts, with Unison claiming the arrangements could leave some workers earning up to £80 less per shift than under previous arrangements

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Company fined £600k after man killed by falling truck he was changing tyres on beside M56 21-year-old Niall Fawcett had been in his role less than four months when tragedy struck Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Report A tyre firm has been hit with a six-figure fine after one of its employees was killed by a falling truck while changing the tyre on a truck at the side of the M56 Niall Fawcett, 21, had been in his role at Lodge Tyre Company Limited - now known as Halford Commercial Fleet Services, a subsidiary of Halfords - for less than four months when he was called out to replace a blown-out tyre on the slip road at junction 7 of the M56 near Bowdon on While positioned below the truck, which was said to be low profile, it slipped from the jack holding it up and landed on Mr Fawcett, tragically causing fatal injuries The Health and Safety Executive said that Mr Fawcett's employer 'had not properly assessed the risks' associated with replacing tyres on a low-profile vehicle Halford Commercial Fleet Services Limited, of Icknield Street Drive, Washford West, Redditch, Worcestershire B98 0DE, pleaded guilty to breaching Section 2(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 at Warrington Magistrates' Court yesterday (November 3)

He spent hours playing in the streets of North Reddish , where he was brought up A big Manchester City fan, he played for his school at Stockport County's Edgeley Park and represented Stockport schoolboys. However, he says, by his late teens, 'reality started to hit' and he realised he would need to 'get into the world of work.' Aged just 18, he got a Saturday job at the BrightHouse furniture shop in Hyde , Tameside . It was the start of a remarkable career journey that has now seen him build his own empire of shops Dad-of-two James, now aged 38, is the founder of Mintro, which buys and sells pre-owned phones and technology, jewellery, watches and designer handbags, and which now has eight stores across the North West, including five in Greater Manchester He has done so alongside a fruitful football career which has seen him play for a number of local non-league sides, most notably Bury FC

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Money Manchester firm that took £123,000 from struggling businesses shut down The firm wrongly told companies that they could avoid reputational damage by selling their companies before liquidation - while charging fees of up to £6,800 Add to preferre A Manchester firm that took £123,000 from 51 struggling businesses was shut down by the High Court on Thursday (October 29). Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of companies with debts by providing 'misleading services', the government's Insolvency Service has said The Manchester-registered company was found to be offering 'alternatives' to formal insolvency to directors of the companies in financial difficulty. It offered to arrange sales of 'financially distressed' businesses for £1 whilst charging fees of between £2,500 and £6,800 It comes following an Insolvency Service investigation which has subsequently led to the firm being shut down Insolvency Service Chief Investigator, David Usher, said: "Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of struggling businesses by offering directors a misleading route out of their company’s debts, charging thousands of pounds for the service "Selling a company does not prevent its former directors’ conduct from being investigated if it later enters liquidation

evidence_packet.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

Altrincham BID, the organisation behind Visit Altrincham, has teamed up with the Little Green Sock Project to bring its Magical Christmas Gift Appeal to the town. The initiative will see Christmas trees appear in shops and businesses across Altrincham, each decorated with special gift tags representing a local child who might otherwise go without a present this Christmas. Customers, staff and visitors are invited to take a tag from one of the trees, buy the gift listed and return it unwrapped to the participating business. The Little Green Sock Project will then collect the presents, match them with children referred to the charity by trusted local professionals and ensure they are delivered in time for Christmas. All donated gifts must be returned before November 30. Jake Shoes was the first Altrincham business to put up its Magical Christmas Tree, with more now appearing across the town. Among the businesses taking part are Altytude Fitness, Aura Music Academy, Bridgfords Estate Agents, Circle Funerals, Goose Green Dental, Jake Shoes, Lund Bennett Law, Mabel's Cafe & Tea Room, Mathnasium of Altrincham, Myerson Solicitors, Oyez Arts at Altrincham Town Hall, Physical Fitness, Santander, Tesco Extra and The

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who drugged and raped his wife for more than 20 years could turn in a minute from an apparently loving husband into a "monster", a court has heard The man, in his 60s, from Stockport, has admitted committing the offences against his wife without her knowledge and allowing other men to engage in sexual activity with her at their marital home He will give evidence against nine men on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court who are alleged to have indulged in the same "barbaric fantasies" Continuing her opening of the prosecution case, Louise Oakley KC showed jurors a series of photographs from summer 2025 of the couple sitting on a garden sofa Oakley said: "They have their arms wrapped around each other and are smiling. They look a normal, happy couple "That, you may think, is the imagery that sums up his depravity. He can be like that one minute and then the next be the monster we have seen on many, many occasions

evidence_packet.lead: Two men, in their 50s and 60s, have been arrested on suspicion of witness intimidation, perverting the course of justice and fraud by the abuse of position after raids in Bolton and South Yorkshire, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said One of the men was previously arrested on su
evidence_packet.summary: Two men, in their 50s and 60s, have been arrested on suspicion of witness intimidation, perverting the course of justice and fraud by the abuse of position after raids in Bolton and South Yorkshire, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said One of the men was previously arrested on su
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two men, in their 50s and 60s, have been arrested on suspicion of witness intimidation, perverting the course of justice and fraud by the abuse of position after raids in Bolton and South Yorkshire, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said One of the men was previously arrested on suspicion of money laundering in July, along with another man and a woman GMP said it was "exploring evidence indicating over £1m worth of fraudulent activity", including 60 transactions and more than a million emails The force started the investigation last year into "serious allegations of fraud and bribery" at the university after a report by the Manchester Mill and a subsequent report from Price Waterhouse Cooper commissioned by the university's Fraud Response Panel Two men in their 60s and a woman in her 50s who were arrested in July were released on bail under investigation Det Insp Matthew Donnelly said it was a "complex and extensive investigation"

Avoidable single-use plastics have been removed from all event sites, the pyrotechnics supplier uses sustainable packaging, and post-event litter picks will take place immediately after the celebrations. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян, один из самых ярких представителей современной русскоязычной стендап-сцены, приглашает вас на свой новый сольный концерт. Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. Не пропустите возможность провести вечер в компании одного из самых самобытных комиков своего поколения. Живой стендап, новые шутки и атмосфера, которую невозможно передать через экран. Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. Саша даёт концерты в столице и ездит в туры, где лично общается со зрителями, устраивает юмористические перформансы и рассказывает шутки о бывшей, путешествиях и трудностях в жизни. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. READ MORE: ANS Group reports 500% RoI from latest AI deployment Students were more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI, including its ability to improve productivity, support learning and reduce workloads. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester FinTech Crediflow AI secures £1.5m Posted on November 4, 2026 by staff Manchester FinTech Crediflow AI secures £1.5m Startup which came through PXN’s PraeSeed programme last year aims to cut manual work behind commercial lending through automation Share: Listen to article FinTech Investment A FinTech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million in funding. Manchester-based Crediflow AI automates the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. The company has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts – a process the industry calls financial spreading – analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital. Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: 27 ноября 2026 года в Studio 338 состоится концерт VOLKANOV в Лондоне Первый вечерний туман над Темзой, отражение городских огней на воде, аромат кофе из маленьких лондонских кофейных и спешка многолюдных улиц — всё это обладает удивительной способностью вдруг остановить время и вернуть к самым ценным воспоминаниям. Так рождаются чувства, которые д Лондон — город, где встречаются десятки культур, языков и человеческих историй, где старинные набережные Темзы соседствуют с современными кварталами, а бешеный ритм мегаполиса не мешает беречь особую атмосферу уюта. В конце ноября именно здесь, вдали от дома, искренние композиции Концерты Дмитрия Волканова — это искренняя встреча, где между артистом и слушателями почти не остается дистанции.
